Math 638 - Homework 8.1¶

A Two-Mode Diffusion Generator¶

This report presents the completed Homework 8.1 experiment.

The data distribution has two one-dimensional modes at

$$ y_1=-2 $$

and

$$ y_2=2. $$

The component standard deviation at the data end is

$$ \sigma_0=0.25. $$

The project follows the density from a two-mode data distribution to a standard Gaussian, derives the exact score, reverses the dynamics, studies mode merging, fits an approximate score network, audits an LLM reverse-time derivation, and analyzes the endpoint loss of latent-mode information.

Executive Summary¶

The forward density is

$$ p_t(x) = \frac{1}{2}N(x;-\alpha(t)A,\sigma(t)^2) + \frac{1}{2}N(x;\alpha(t)A,\sigma(t)^2), $$

with

$$ A=2 $$

and

$$ \alpha(t)=\cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{2}\right). $$

The variance schedule is

$$ \sigma(t)^2 = 1-(1-\sigma_0^2)\alpha(t)^2. $$

At $t=0$ the density is sharply concentrated near $-2$ and $2$.

At $t=1$ both components become the same standard Gaussian.

The final compiled results support the following conclusions:

  • the chosen schedule satisfies the required marginal equations;
  • the analytic mixture score agrees with a numerical derivative of $\log p_t$;
  • the two visible density peaks merge at approximately $t=0.702823$;
  • the reverse-time sign is correct and independently validated on a centered Gaussian;
  • exact-score reverse generation reproduces the two-mode target accurately;
  • visible bimodality and latent-component distinguishability are different concepts;
  • the fitted neural score works but is measurably worse than the exact score;
  • the fitted network reached its 60-epoch training budget while validation MSE was still improving;
  • the final density is smooth even though the mixture representation becomes unidentifiable;
  • the latent component-label information approaches zero at the final Gaussian endpoint.

Validity Audit¶

All ten submitted notebooks contain executed code cells with no recorded cell errors.

The numerical outputs agree with the mathematical derivations.

The main audit correction concerns Task 3, where a generic peak finder originally split the flat critical maximum into two adjacent numerical peaks. The corrected result records one central maximum at the analytic merge threshold.

The main experimental limitation is Task 7. The best validation MSE occurs at epoch 60, which is the maximum allowed training epoch. Therefore the fitted score is a finite-budget approximation and should not be described as fully converged.

A small presentation issue was also corrected in this final report: two escaped symbols in the reflection source were converted to literal tab characters. The intended expressions are rendered correctly here as $\tau$ and $\times$.

No reverse-time sign error, data leakage, endpoint-density singularity, or incompatibility between the chosen marginal schedule and forward SDE was found.

Task 1 - Schedule, Forward Dynamics, and Density Evolution¶

Choose

$$ T=1, $$

$$ \alpha(t) = \cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{2}\right), $$

and

$$ q=1-\sigma_0^2. $$

Then

$$ \sigma(t)^2 = 1-q\alpha(t)^2. $$

The compatible affine forward drift is

$$ f(x,t)=b(t)x, $$

where

$$ b(t) = -\frac{\pi}{2} \tan\left(\frac{\pi t}{2}\right), $$

and the diffusion coefficient satisfies

$$ g(t)^2 = \pi \tan\left(\frac{\pi t}{2}\right). $$

For $t<1$, these satisfy

$$ \alpha'(t)=b(t)\alpha(t) $$

and

$$ \frac{d}{dt}\sigma(t)^2 = 2b(t)\sigma(t)^2+g(t)^2. $$

The coefficients diverge as $t$ approaches 1, but the density remains regular. Numerical SDE evaluation is therefore avoided exactly at the singular coefficient endpoint, while the exact limiting density is retained.

The maximum saved residuals are

$$ 4.441e-16 $$

for the alpha equation and

$$ 2.980e-08 $$

for the variance equation.

The second residual comes from subtracting very large terms close to the singular coefficient endpoint and remains negligible relative to those coefficient magnitudes.

Task 2 - Exact Score¶

Let

$$ m(t)=A\alpha(t) $$

and

$$ v(t)=\sigma(t)^2. $$

For the positive-mean component, the posterior responsibility is

$$ r_+(x,t) = \frac{1}{2} \left( 1+ \tanh\left( \frac{m(t)x}{v(t)} \right) \right). $$

The exact score is

$$ s(x,t) = \frac{ m(t) \tanh\left( \frac{m(t)x}{v(t)} \right) -x }{ v(t) }. $$

At the final endpoint,

$$ m(1)=0, $$

$$ v(1)=1, $$

and therefore

$$ s(x,1)=-x. $$

Finite-difference validation of the exact score¶

The largest finite-difference RMSE occurs at the sharply concentrated data endpoint and is about $7.89\times 10^{-5}$. The discrepancy rapidly decreases as the density becomes smoother.

Task 3 - Score Geometry and Mode Merging¶

For the equal symmetric mixture, the modality change occurs when

$$ m(t)^2=v(t). $$

The density has two distinct visible maxima when

$$ m(t)>\sqrt{v(t)}. $$

With the selected schedule, the critical time is approximately

$$ t_{merge}=0.702823. $$

At the equality case, the center is a degenerate flat maximum. It should be counted as one central maximum, not two nearby numerical maxima.

Before the critical time, the density has two visible maxima. After the critical time it is unimodal, even though the latent mixture still contains two component labels before the final merger.

Therefore two mixture components do not imply two visible density peaks.

Task 4 - Reverse Probability Flow and Sign Audit¶

The forward probability-flow equation is

$$ \frac{dX_t}{dt} = f(X_t,t) - \frac{1}{2}g(t)^2s(X_t,t). $$

Use the increasing reverse clock

$$ \tau=1-t. $$

Then

$$ \frac{dX}{d\tau} = -\frac{dX}{dt}. $$

After analytically cancelling the singular endpoint terms, the probability-flow velocity has a continuous endpoint limit.

The reverse-clock implementation is checked independently on a centered Gaussian. Reverse generation must contract the variance from 1 to $\sigma_0^2$.

tau t Drift at x=1 Drift at x=-1 Positive contracts Negative contracts
0.05 0.95 -0.115853 0.115853 True True
0.25 0.75 -0.603508 0.603508 True True
0.50 0.50 -1.385997 1.385997 True True
0.75 0.25 -2.605940 2.605940 True True
0.95 0.05 -1.687162 1.687162 True True

The centered-Gaussian RK4 validation gives

$$ RMSE = 6.568e-13. $$

The maximum absolute sample-map error is

$$ 2.244e-12. $$

This independently supports the reverse-time sign convention.

Task 5 - Exact Reverse Generation¶

Reverse generation begins from the exact endpoint distribution

$$ X_1\sim N(0,1). $$

The target at $t=0$ is

$$ \frac{1}{2}N(-2,0.25^2) + \frac{1}{2}N(2,0.25^2). $$

The exact target moments are

$$ E[X]=0, $$

$$ Var(X)=4.0625, $$

and

$$ E[X^4]=17.51171875. $$

Ten thousand standard-Gaussian samples are transported backward with the exact score.

The histogram comparison shows that exact-score reverse generation reproduces both target clusters.

Task 6 - Separation, Bimodality, and Latent Labels¶

At the data endpoint, let the component means be $-a$ and $a$ with standard deviation $\sigma_0$.

The total separation is

$$ d=2a. $$

Visible bimodality occurs exactly when

$$ a>\sigma_0, $$

or equivalently

$$ \frac{d}{\sigma_0}>2. $$

The optimal Bayes error for the latent component label is

$$ P_{error} = \Phi\left( -\frac{d}{2\sigma_0} \right). $$

Unlike visible bimodality, label distinguishability has no sharp transition at $d/\sigma_0=2$.

d / sigma0 Numerical peaks Bayes label error Bayes label accuracy

1.0 1 0.308538 0.691462
1.5 1 0.226627 0.773373
2.0 1 0.158655 0.841345
2.5 2 0.105650 0.894350

16.0 2 0.000000 1.000000

At the visible-bimodality threshold $d/\sigma_0=2$, the optimal latent-label accuracy is already about 84.1 percent.

This directly demonstrates that visible peaks and statistical distinguishability are different properties.

Task 7 - Fitted Score Network¶

The exact score is replaced by a small neural approximation trained with exact-score supervision.

The objective is

$$ L(\theta) = E[ (s_\theta(X_t,t)-s(X_t,t))^2 ]. $$

The architecture is

$$ s_\theta(x,t) = -x + (1-t)^2R_\theta(x,t). $$

This enforces the exact endpoint condition

$$ s_\theta(x,1)=-x. $$

Odd symmetry in $x$ is not imposed.

Training, validation, held-out test, generation noise, and target-reference samples use separate seeds. The held-out test set is created only after validation-based model selection.

The held-out score metrics are:

  • test samples: 16000;
  • RMSE: 0.166646;
  • MAE: 0.101427;
  • maximum absolute error: 3.188103.

The best saved validation MSE is

$$ 0.029278 $$

at epoch

$$ 60. $$

Because epoch 60 is the maximum training budget and validation MSE was still decreasing, this result is a finite-budget approximation. It does not establish optimization convergence.

Method Samples Mean Variance Left mass Wasserstein KS KS p-value Paired RMSE vs exact
exact_score 3000 -0.034427 4.089048 0.508667 0.025366 0.015866 0.432465 0.000000
fitted_score 3000 -0.005393 4.086442 0.504000 0.038376 0.045757 6.75946e-06 0.158690

The fitted-score generator preserves approximately balanced mode mass and approximately correct variance, but it is measurably worse than exact-score generation.

The fitted-score KS statistic is about 0.0458, compared with about 0.0159 for the exact score.

The paired fitted-versus-exact output RMSE is about 0.1587.

Therefore mode balance alone is not sufficient evidence that a learned score field is accurate.

Held-out score predictions are compared directly with the exact analytic labels.

Task 8 - LLM Reverse-Dynamics Audit¶

The LLM was asked to derive the reverse-time SDE and the probability-flow ODE while stating the time convention explicitly.

For the decreasing original-time convention, the recorded reverse-SDE drift was

$$ f-g^2s. $$

For the increasing reverse clock

$$ \tau=T-t, $$

the recorded reverse-SDE drift was

$$ -f+g^2s. $$

The forward probability-flow drift was

$$ f-\frac{1}{2}g^2s, $$

so the increasing reverse-clock probability-flow drift was

$$ -f+\frac{1}{2}g^2s. $$

These signs are correct.

Formula tested Drift at x=1, t=0.5 Contracts positive x
correct reverse-clock probability flow -1.385997 True
wrong score sign probability flow 4.527589 False
correct reverse-clock SDE -4.342790 True
wrong score sign SDE 7.484382 False

The centered-Gaussian test is a useful independent sign audit.

With the correct score sign, the reverse-clock drift points inward at positive $x$.

With the opposite sign, the drift points outward.

For the reverse SDE this is a statement about the deterministic drift only. Brownian noise remains present, so an individual stochastic path is not required to move inward at every instant.

Task 9 - The Merging Singularity¶

As $t$ approaches 1,

$$ \alpha(t)\to 0, $$

$$ \sigma(t)^2\to 1, $$

and

$$ s(x,t)\to -x. $$

The positive-component responsibility satisfies

$$ r_+(x,t)\to \frac{1}{2}. $$

The density becomes the smooth standard Gaussian.

At the same time, the two latent component labels become statistically indistinguishable.

The latent-label mutual information falls from approximately

$$ \log(2)=0.6931 $$

nats at the data endpoint to approximately

$$ 4.93\times 10^{-4} $$

nats at $t=0.99$, and to numerical zero at the endpoint.

Three different phenomena must therefore be distinguished:

  1. the final density is smooth and nonsingular;
  2. the chosen finite-endpoint SDE coefficients are singular;
  3. the two-component representation becomes unidentifiable.

After analytic cancellation, the stabilized probability-flow velocity has a regular endpoint limit.

The information-loss curve makes the representation singularity quantitative.

Final Reflection¶

This experiment shows how a single simple noise distribution can correspond to several structured outcomes under reverse diffusion.

At $t=1$, the two mixture components have merged into the same standard Gaussian. The density is smooth, the exact score is

$$ s(x,1)=-x, $$

and the latent component label is no longer identifiable.

Task 9 makes this loss of information quantitative. The latent-label mutual information falls from approximately 0.6931 nats at $t=0$ to approximately $4.93\times 10^{-4}$ nats at $t=0.99$, and it is numerically zero at the endpoint. The endpoint singularity is therefore not a singular probability density. It is a loss of identifiability in the mixture representation together with singular coefficients in the chosen finite-time SDE schedule.

The score field supplies the geometry needed to unfold the final Gaussian. Tasks 2 and 3 verify the score and show how its stationary points change when the two visible density peaks merge. For the selected parameters, the analytic merge time is about $t=0.702823$. Before that time the density has two distinct maxima; afterward it is unimodal even though the latent mixture still has two component labels before the endpoint. Task 6 gives the same lesson from another direction: visible bimodality occurs only when $d/\sigma_0>2$, while latent labels can already be statistically distinguishable below that threshold.

The reverse-time sign is essential. Using the increasing reverse clock

$$ \tau=1-t, $$

the reverse probability-flow drift has the opposite time orientation from the forward flow. The centered-Gaussian test verifies that reverse generation contracts the variance from 1 to $\sigma_0^2$. The RK4 map agrees with the exact centered-Gaussian map with RMSE about $6.57\times 10^{-13}$. The LLM sign audit reaches the same sign convention independently.

With the exact score, reverse generation accurately reproduces the two-mode target. For 10,000 samples and 1,000 RK4 steps, the generated mean is about $-0.0282$, variance about 4.0514 compared with the exact value 4.0625, and left-mode mass 0.5074 compared with the target 0.5. The KS statistic is about 0.0110 and the Wasserstein distance to an independent target sample is about 0.0113. Refining the RK4 step size from $1/250$ to $1/2000$ changes these values negligibly.

Replacing the exact score by a learned score makes the experiment more realistic and exposes a second source of error. The held-out score RMSE is about 0.1666. Starting exact-score and fitted-score reverse flows from the same 3,000 Gaussian samples, the fitted model has a KS statistic about 0.0458 compared with about 0.0159 for the exact score. The paired fitted-versus-exact sample RMSE is about 0.1587. Its mode mass remains close to one half, but that does not prove that the learned vector field is accurate.

The neural result also has an important training limitation. Validation MSE was still improving at epoch 60, which was the declared maximum training budget. The saved fitted score should therefore be interpreted as a budget-limited approximation rather than a fully converged optimum.

Overall, this two-mode example captures the essential geometry of diffusion generation. Forward dynamics erase visible modal structure until the data become ordinary Gaussian noise. Reverse generation uses the score field to reconstruct a distribution over structured outcomes. The endpoint noise does not retain an observable unique component label. Generation succeeds by transforming the full distribution, not by recovering a latent label that remains directly readable in the noise.

Overall Conclusion¶

Homework 8.1 demonstrates the full two-mode diffusion pipeline from structured data to noise and back.

The main conclusions are:

  • the selected forward schedule is mathematically compatible with the prescribed marginals;
  • the density remains smooth while the visible modes merge;
  • the exact score correctly captures the changing density geometry;
  • the reverse-time sign must be handled together with the chosen time convention;
  • exact-score reverse generation accurately reconstructs the two-mode target;
  • visible bimodality is not equivalent to latent-component distinguishability;
  • learned-score quality must be evaluated by score error and generation discrepancy, not only by mode balance;
  • the final Gaussian hides the original component identity even though reverse dynamics can generate the correct multimodal distribution;
  • the representation becomes singular before the probability density itself becomes singular.

The experiment therefore provides a small but rigorous model of the central diffusion-model idea: a simple noise distribution can be transformed into a structured multimodal distribution when the reverse dynamics use the correct score field.
